LanguageData.RK_Bounty.Tale_IssueSuccess_0: The hunting party of {FACTION} kept their word. They picked up {THING}'s trail in a rainstorm and followed it for two days - blood on the mud, cold campfire ash - until they laid their trap just beyond the picket lines of {TARGETFAC}. The fight lasted from dusk until deep in the night: ropes, snares, tranq darts, and one well-placed pellet of shot. The lead hunter has been boasting about it in taverns for a week, but the paper they hand you says only one cold line: charges, {CRIME}. The agreed fee: {REWARD} silver.
LanguageData.RK_Bounty.Tale_IssueSuccess_1: This warrant circulated through the hunter guilds of {FACTION} for a long while before a veteran crew took it. Disguised as pilgrims, they walked into a {TARGETFAC} market and did the job in broad daylight - so fast the local guards never even reacted. Three days later, road-worn hunters appeared at the edge of your colony with {THING} strapped to a cargo board. The leader brushed the dust off his hands and grinned: "Clean work. Fair price." {REWARD} silver, counted on the spot.
LanguageData.RK_Bounty.Tale_IssueSuccess_2: {FACTION} never swung a blade themselves - they subcontracted the warrant to the meanest band of sellswords on the frontier. It was money well spent: {THING} was cornered in a dead-end valley with the escape route buried under rockfall and the way forward bristling with poisoned arrows. The paperwork says {CRIME} - but mercenaries don't ask reasons, only about the bounty, and they don't listen to begging. When their courier knocked on your door, what he carried over his shoulder was exactly what you paid for. The invoice for {REWARD} silver came with a note: "Got another job? Call us."
LanguageData.RK_Bounty.Tale_IssueOutLiving: {THING} is still alive - bound tight, the sedative not yet fully worn off. Pay {REWARD} silver and the hunters will hand it over, transport insurance included.
LanguageData.RK_Bounty.Tale_IssueOutDead: {THING} is dead. The hunters underestimated its final frenzy and brought the body back anyway - by guild rules, a corpse is only worth {REWARD} silver.
LanguageData.RK_Bounty.Tale_IssueFail_0: Bad news. The hunting party of {FACTION} chased {THING} for two full weeks, from jungle to tundra, and lost the trail at the very last step. They came back to their base with empty packs and feet more blistered than their pockets were full. The leader's letter to you was short: the target is gone, the advance will not be refunded. Worse, the failed expedition burned through gear - and the guild's ledger has quietly written the resentment under your name.
LanguageData.RK_Bounty.Tale_IssueFail_1: The hunters of {FACTION} kicked a hornet's nest this time. Pieced together from survivors: their ambush on {THING} inside {TARGETFAC} territory was flawless - right up until the target produced something nobody had planned for. The crew lost nearly half its members and limped back across the border, and the guild's reputation sank with them. The guild sent the bill to whoever posted the warrant: the advance is forfeit, and the grudge is fresh. The charge of "{CRIME}" on the warrant is now the only footnote to this whole farce.
LanguageData.RK_Bounty.Tale_IssueFail_2: The crew that took your warrant from {FACTION} has dissolved. It started as a quarrel over the split: some thought {THING} wasn't worth the fee, others simply vanished with the shared gear. When {FACTION} sent inspectors, only ash and a few half-burnt ropes remained of the camp. Nobody won this farce - your advance payment is gone, and the guild refuses to hear anything more about the warrant on {TARGETFAC} (charges: {CRIME}).
LanguageData.RK_Bounty.Tale_TakeSuccess_Pawn_Text:
The handover was finished at dawn. As [victim_nameFull] was marched through the gate of [asker_faction_name]'s outpost, the guards' cheering startled a whole flock of birds. [asker_nameFull] inspected everything personally, then pressed a seal into the papers: charges of [reason], warrant withdrawn, bounty payable.

Payment follows the condition of the delivery: [rewardForLiving] silver for a living captive, [rewardForDead] for a corpse. The clerk riding along added one piece of advice: "If another commission from [asker_faction_name] reaches you, don't hesitate."

On the road home, you could swear the watchtowers of [victim_faction_name] had a few more eyes on them than before. The bounty market has no pity for failures - and you were not one.
LanguageData.RK_Bounty.Tale_TakeSuccess_Animal_Text:
The blood on the hide had not yet dried. [victim_nameFull]'s carcass was butchered, lashed, and loaded onto the last pack animal of the caravan, bumping along all the way to the outpost of [asker_faction_name].

[asker_nameFull] circled the kill three times, checked the wounds under the hide, and finally nodded in satisfaction. The hunters collected the [rewardForDead] silver bounty, and from that day the tavern had a story worth telling for ten years: the beast that nearly flipped the whole wagon.

Back at your colony, someone slipped a note through the door crack: "Next time, don't drag the kill in quite so bloody." - unsigned.
LanguageData.RK_Bounty.Tale_TakeSuccess_Tame_Text:
When [animal_indefinite] trotted placidly through the outpost gate behind your animal handler, the gatekeeper of [asker_faction_name] rubbed his eyes three times before he believed them.

[asker_nameFull] paid the [reward] silver bounty on the spot, then ordered it led into a specially built pen - they say the man had gone half grey over this one animal. At parting he pressed a beast-shaped badge into your hand: "The gates of [asker_faction_name] will always stand open to those who understand wild things."

All the way home, your handler hummed to himself. You couldn't tell whether it was the silver that pleased him, or the animal.
LanguageData.RK_Bounty.Tale_TakeSuccess_Artifact_Text:
[artifactLabel] glowed faintly in the candlelight. [asker_nameFull] held it and studied it for a long time, fingers almost afraid to grip - as if the slightest pressure might shatter that buried history all over again.

"You cannot imagine what this means to [asker_faction_name]." The [reward] silver arrived as promised, and for once the thank-you that came with it did not sound like courtesy.

As you left, the guard captain quietly told you that three parties had already died for this thing. You swallowed your own remark and took only the money.
LanguageData.RK_Bounty.Tale_TakeFail_Pawn_Text:
[asker_faction_name] has taken down the wanted notice for [victim_nameFull] - pinned, together with the charges of [reason], to the expired section of the board.

[asker_nameFull]'s last letter reads: "The deadline has passed. From this day, this person's whereabouts are no longer our concern." The bounty is void - and word on the border grows uglier: they say [victim_nameFull] is telling anyone who will listen a story about "betrayal".

The bounty market has no tears. Only the next notice, and the next purse.
LanguageData.RK_Bounty.Tale_TakeFail_Animal_Text:
The herd has moved on. When your hunters finally reached the valley of the rumors, all that remained was stripped brushwood and a few cold tracks.

[asker_faction_name] waited fifteen days, then withdrew the [rewardForDead] silver bounty. [asker_nameFull]'s reply was ice: "Prey waits for no one."

Only the hunters themselves knew that the beast's trail once came within a single river of your camp. So close - and on the hunting grounds, every story is forever just that one step short.
LanguageData.RK_Bounty.Tale_TakeFail_Tame_Text:
For fifteen days the tamers of [asker_faction_name] waited, and all they received was a formal explanation: that [animal_indefinite] proved warier than anything on record - three approaches, three slipped snares, and finally a disappearance into a canyon no map has ever named.

[asker_nameFull] withdrew the [reward] silver bounty. They say he was so disappointed he fired half his stable hands that same evening.

That is how it goes between hunters and wild things - no purse, however full, can ever buy a second chance.
LanguageData.RK_Bounty.Tale_TakeFail_Artifact_Text:
The camp that held [artifactLabel] vanished from the map after one night of heavy rain - the treasure, the guards, and every thread leading to it. By the time your people arrived, nothing remained but a marsh waist-deep in black water.

[asker_faction_name] withdrew the [reward] silver bounty per the contract. [asker_nameFull]'s letter was short: "The trail is broken. This thing and I were never meant to meet."

New stories are already spreading along the trade roads: some say it was seen in the far north, some say it never existed at all. The ink on the notice board has dried - the story is only just beginning.
LanguageData.RK_Bounty.Tale_Accept_0: A road-worn courier knocked on your door and handed over a wax-sealed letter. The hunter guild of {FACTION} has deliberated and formally accepted the job of hunting down {THING}.\n\n"We make our living at this," the hunt-leader wrote. "The lands of {TARGETFAC} are hard to enter, but the purse is enough to buy informants on three trade roads. We will write when there is progress." Enclosed was a copy of the contract - your name circled in red ink.
LanguageData.RK_Bounty.Tale_Accept_1: Late at night, your comms console crackled to life. The voice on the other end spoke low and gave a codename only: the warrant-taker of {FACTION}. "Your bounty - we'll take it. Don't ask who we are. Watch the results."\n\nThe plan, in brief: learn {THING}'s routines within {TARGETFAC} territory first, then choose a moment to strike. "This one's promising," the voice added before signing off. "The target has made enemies lately - and you're not the only ones."
LanguageData.RK_Bounty.Tale_Track_0: The hunting party of {FACTION} sent their first good news. On the {TARGETFAC} border they found signs of {THING} at an abandoned campsite - a fire not long dead, discarded bandages, and half-buried papers bearing an old name.\n\n"The target is wary, but does not yet know it is being hunted." The courier relayed the hunt-leader's words. "Our informant network is open. Have the balance ready - we do not sell half-finished work."
LanguageData.RK_Bounty.Tale_Track_1: The hunters laid eyes on {THING} for the first time - in a market deep in {TARGETFAC} territory, across a pressing crowd. Moving openly there was too risky, so the party chose to shadow instead.\n\nThey lost the trail once, but a local informant picked it up again two days later. {FACTION}'s letter was meant to reassure you: "The prey has caught the wind - but it will not slip through our hands."
LanguageData.RK_Bounty.Tale_Clash_0: The noose has closed. The hunting party of {FACTION} has {THING} cornered with nowhere left to run - and the letter summed up what followed in a single line: "Contact. The target is tougher than expected. We've taken losses, but the ring is complete."\n\nAt the end, the hunt-leader reminded you: have the agreed payment ready - delivery is days away. Beneath the fatigue between the lines, you could almost hear the triumph.
LanguageData.RK_Bounty.Tale_Clash_1: {THING} tried to break out last night and ran straight into the pickets {FACTION} had laid. After a short, sharp chase, the ring tightened by another notch.\n\nBut for once the hunt-leader's letter carried worry: {TARGETFAC} reinforcements may already be on the road, and time is running short. "These last few days - we either finish the job, or walk away," it ended. "Either way, you will have your answer."
LanguageData.RK_Bounty.Tale_IssueSuccess_3: The hunters of {FACTION} chose a moonless night. They slipped past three of {TARGETFAC}'s picket lines in the dark and waited outside {THING}'s shelter until the small hours - the strike itself was quick as a silent collapse; by the time the sentries noticed anything, the party was already on the way out.\n\n"Night-hunting is our family trade," the leader allowed himself at the handover. Charges, {CRIME}. Fee, {REWARD} silver, stamped with the guild's seal.
LanguageData.RK_Bounty.Tale_IssueSuccess_4: Nobody expected the job to be finished by one of {TARGETFAC}'s own. Someone inside with a long-held grudge sold {THING}'s whereabouts to {FACTION} - the price, they say, was nothing more than a passage out.\n\nThe hunters followed the map and met almost no real resistance. The paperwork delivered to you is deliberately understated: charges, {CRIME}; fee, {REWARD} silver. Only one small line is worth chewing on: "The strongest fortress always opens from within."
LanguageData.RK_Bounty.Tale_IssueFail_3: The hunters of {FACTION} struck empty air. By the time the ring closed on {THING}'s last known hideout, all that remained was a pot of still-warm stew and a bedroll packed in haste - someone had tipped the target off.\n\nThree days of pursuit later, the trail died inside {TARGETFAC} territory. The hunt-leader's letter carried rare apology: "We own this one. The advance is forfeit by guild law - but the next job, you get twenty percent off."
LanguageData.RK_Bounty.Tale_IssueFail_4: This one was lost to the weather. The party from {FACTION} closed on {THING} three times, and three times the sky broke it up - flash floods washed out the tracks, mudslides cut the pass, and in the fog even the hunters lost each other.\n\nWhen the storm finally passed, the target was gone. The guild's closing statement was all officialese: "Act of God." But at the bottom, one line that didn't sound official at all: "This land protects its own. Next time, pick a better season."

LanguageData.RK_SkyNet.Stage1Text: A long-range array caught a rhythmic digital pulse — something is mapping this world. The resistance warns: Skynet has noticed you. Prepare.
LanguageData.RK_SkyNet.Stage2Text: The metal legion doubled its activity; infiltrators already walk among people. The resistance asks for your help — the more you cull, the slower their mastermind arrives.
LanguageData.RK_SkyNet.Stage3Text: Final intel from the resistance: a T-X prototype terminatrix is coming — Skynet's hub on this front. Destroy it; the bounty and the tech wreckage are yours.
LanguageData.RK_SkyNet.RewardText: The T-X terminatrix crumples, sparks fading. The resistance credits you for the kill (goodwill and recognition up) and hands over {0} pieces of Skynet tech wreckage as thanks.

LanguageData.RK_Bounty.Alert_NoCommsFacilityText: Your colony has no communications facility yet — build either a bird post or a comms console. The bird post is the hub for bounty contracts and warrants (without it, new bounties cannot arrive and warrants cannot be sent; keep it fed, or the birds refuse to fly). The comms console is your lifeline to the outside (with no powered console, orbital drop-offs, calling caravans and contacting factions are all unavailable, and captured bounty targets must travel on foot or by caravan escort). Either one is enough.
LanguageData.RK_Bounty.Alert_NoCommsFacilityText_Rese: Your colony has no communications facility yet — build either a bird post or a comms console, but neither is unlocked: complete research "{0}" first. The bird post handles bounty contracts and warrants; the comms console is your lifeline for orbital drop-offs, calling caravans and contacting factions.
